data.title: Glossary of the Week
data.subtitle: Key Terms in Uzbekistan's Legal History

narr: Now let's explore some key terms that have shaped Uzbekistan's legal history.
These concepts span from ancient legal sources to modern constitutional developments.

rows.text: Constitution (Konstitutsiya)
the fundamental law of the state; the Constitution of Uzbekistan of 1992 legally formalized the formation of a sovereign democratic state
Constitutional Commission
established in 1990 with 64 members under the chairmanship of I. A. Karimov; from July 2–3, 1992 — 71 members; working group — 32 people
Declaration of Independence
adopted on June 20, 1990 by the second session of the Supreme Council of the 12th convocation
Law 'On the Foundations of State Independence'
constitutional law of August 31, 1991 consisting of 17 articles — the legal foundation of independence
Nationwide Discussion
discussion of the Constitution draft from September 26 to early December 1992; for the first time conducted in two stages (second publication — November 21, 1992)
Presumption of Innocence
principle enshrined in Art. 26 of the Constitution on the proposal of the chairman of the commission

narr: Let's start with terms related to Uzbekistan's independence and constitutional development.
The Constitution is the fundamental law of the state, with the 1992 Constitution formalizing Uzbekistan's sovereignty.
The Constitutional Commission was established in 1990, initially with 64 members under I. A. Karimov.
The Declaration of Independence was adopted on June 20, 1990, while the Law on the Foundations of State Independence came later in 1991.
The Nationwide Discussion of the Constitution draft was conducted in two stages, a first for the country.
The Presumption of Innocence principle was enshrined in Article 26 of the Constitution.
